props.title: You'll Change
lines: Long-term planning is hard because your future self is a stranger.
Avoid extreme plans that only work if you never change your mind.

props.title: You will not want the same life
items: People are very good at guessing how much they have changed — and very bad at guessing they will keep changing.
27% of college graduates work in a job related to their major. Compound that over a career.
Sunk costs of identity: 'I am a person who holds this stock' is a trap when the thesis died.
Prefer balanced plans you can revisit every few years over a 40-year vow made at 22.

props.kicker: YOU WILL NOT STAY THIS PERSON
props.title: The end-of-history illusion

rows.v: Only 27% of college graduates work in a job related to their major. Identity is not a 40-year contract.
'I am a person who holds this stock' is how people refuse to sell a dead thesis.
A 40-year financial vow made at 22 assumes a stranger will thank you. Maybe they will not.
Revisit goals every few years. Moderate plans survive personality drift better than extremes.

props.title: Leave yourself an exit that is not failure
items: Avoid careers, houses, and portfolios that only work if you never change your mind.
Changing a goal is not weakness. Pretending you are finished evolving is.

props.kicker: DO NOT MARRY A PAST GOAL
props.title: Identity is a sunk cost too

rows.v: The end-of-history illusion: you see past change clearly and assume the future you is finished.
Only twenty-seven percent of graduates work in a job related to their major. Careers drift.
I am a person who holds this stock is how a dead thesis gets a second decade.
A forty-year financial vow at twenty-two is a letter to a stranger. Leave a stamp for revisions.
Moderate plans survive personality drift. Extreme plans require you never to grow.
